newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg shares down on competitive concerns.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg shares down on competitive concerns.

text.p: Kellogg Co's share price dropped one point to 66-3/4 on Friday on concerns over the cereal giant's market share and competitive pressure in the U.S. market, analysts said.
Kellogg made a presentation to analysts today.
Smith Barney analyst David Rabinowitz said one concern is the slow growth of the U.S. cereal market, despite price cuts by Kellogg and other cereal makers earlier this year.
Kellogg pledged to take the necessary steps to preserve its roughly one-third share of the U.S. market, but in the short-term it will not resort to deep discounts, analysts said.
Kellogg's U.S. market share is 32.5-33 percent. "They consider 35 percent to be normal," said Schroder Wertheim analyst Robert Cummins.
Rabinowitz said that if Kellogg and other major cereal makers back off from deep-discount promotions, branded cereals could face further competitive pressure from value-priced products.
In its presentation to analysts, Kellogg reiterated that it expects modest earnings growth in the fourth quarter compared with the $0.77 a share it earned in the year-ago period, analysts said.
As reported earlier, Kellogg said first quarter 1997 earnings likely will be down from the $0.99 a share of a year earlier.
Kellogg also said it expects fiscal 1997 earnings will show an increase from 1996, analysts said.
According to First Call, the mean estimate for Kellogg's 1996 earnings is $3.07 a share, compared with $3.48 in 1995. The mean estimate for 1997 is $3.47 a share.
